headline: Celebrity AI deepfakes are racking up millions of views, no one is safe
summary: AI-generated images of Mia Goth on a verified fan account garnered nearly 500,000 likes, while a Taylor Swift deepfake video hit 1.8 million views, highlighting the widespread issue.
details: AI-generated photos and videos of celebrities are gaining millions of views on social media platforms. One instance involved an AI image of actress Mia Goth, posted on a verified fan account, which quickly amassed nearly 500,000 likes.

The account, despite being a fan page, qualified for Instagram's blue "verified" checkmark, which Meta allows users to purchase. Goth's representative had previously complained to Instagram about the account posting "counterfeit, AI images."

This deepfake image spread through celebrity gossip outlets and even influenced Google search results, which generated AI overviews citing these blogs as fact. Instagram eventually removed the account for impersonation.

The problem extends beyond individual cases, with a growing volume of AI content online. Many profiles exclusively post realistic, often sexualized, AI-generated images of female public figures like Scarlett Johansson, Millie Bobby Brown, and Zendaya.

Some accounts use these AI images to advertise adult content off-platform, linking to Patreon and Telegram channels selling subscriptions. Another viral example showed an AI-generated Taylor Swift video with 1.8 million views.

After inquiries from The Verge, Meta removed some of the identified accounts, including those impersonating Mia Goth and Scarlett Johansson. A Meta spokesperson stated that the company does not permit accounts to use someone's likeness to pose as them, regardless of content origin.

headline_marked: [[Tesla Roadster unveiled]] after years of delays, promising 620-mile range and 0-60 in 1.9s
headline: Tesla Roadster unveiled after years of delays, promising 620-mile range and 0-60 in 1.9s
summary: After years of anticipation, Tesla is finally unveiling its second-gen Roadster. It promises a 620-mile range, 0-60 mph in 1.9 seconds, and even hints at cold-gas thrusters and flying capabilities.
details: Tesla is finally unveiling its second-gen Roadster, after nearly nine years since its initial 2017 reveal. The original promises included a 620-mile range and a 0-60 mph acceleration in just 1.9 seconds.
The electric hypercar was initially slated for a 2020 release but faced repeated delays. CEO Elon Musk has been hyping the event on X, calling it a "candidate for greatest product demo of all time."
Recent teasers on Tesla's website suggest the possibility of cold-gas thrusters. There have also been reports hinting at the car's potential ability to fly, adding to the spectacle.
Musk further fueled anticipation by posting that the demo would be a "BANGER," possibly literally. The tech community is watching closely to see if Tesla delivers on these ambitious claims.
caption:
Tesla's second-gen Roadster is finally here, promising a 620-mile range and 0-60 mph in 1.9 seconds. Elon Musk hints at "cold-gas thrusters" and a "banger" demo.

Tesla is finally unveiling its second-gen Roadster, after nearly nine years since its initial 2017 reveal. The original promises included a 620-mile range and a 0-60 mph acceleration in just 1.9 seconds.

The electric hypercar was initially slated for a 2020 release but faced repeated delays. CEO Elon Musk has been hyping the event on X, calling it a "candidate for greatest product demo of all time."

Recent teasers on Tesla's website suggest the possibility of cold-gas thrusters. There have also been reports hinting at the car's potential ability to fly, adding to the spectacle.

Musk further fueled anticipation by posting that the demo would be a "BANGER," possibly literally. The tech community is watching closely to see if Tesla delivers on these ambitious claims.
